title: Jump Game VIII
summary: Given an integer array nums and a cost array costs, both of length n, find the minimum cost to jump from index 0 to index n-1.
statement: Given an integer array nums and a cost array costs, both of length n, find the minimum cost to jump from index 0 to index n-1. You can jump from index i to j if nums[i] nums[j] with all k in i = nums[i]. The cost of jumping to index i is costs[i].
constraints: From i to later j, jump when nums[i]<=nums[j] and every intermediate value is below nums[i], or when nums[i]>nums[j] and every intermediate value is at least nums[i].
Starting at index zero costs nothing; landing at j adds costs[j].
Return the minimum cost to reach the last index.
hints: The only useful predecessors are exposed by two monotonic stacks for the two jump inequalities.
When a new value arrives, each node popped from the non-increasing or increasing stack has a legal direct jump to it.
Relax dp[index] from every popped predecessor on both stacks, then push the index.
Any predecessor hidden deeper is blocked by a nearer value unless it becomes exposed through popping, so all and only potentially optimal jump edges are relaxed.
editorial: Adjacent nodes are exposed by one stack, while any longer legal predecessor is popped at its first qualifying endpoint, so the two stack scans relax all jump choices needed by an optimum.

tests.explanation: The best legal jump sequence reaches the last index with total landing cost eight.
The valid route is zero to one to two, with total landing cost two; the intermediate one blocks a direct jump.
